records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Einen Ton über Licht übertragen
records.summary: The task assesses the exact audio-over-light competence, with a genuine observed-build requirement only in the preselected student-experiment mode. Sender/receiver conversion, path test and fault diagnosis are coherent.
material: Separate5-V supplies and only an optical link support the intended path-isolation test; visible current-limited LED, DC offset, photodiode conversion and speaker chain are sufficiently specified.
A constant intensity cannot carry a sustained periodic audio tone; a switching transient is explicitly distinguished.
solution: 401±3 Hz gives[398,404] and798±4 gives[794,802], both containing the respective input400/800 Hz.
Optical interruption supports the chosen signal path but does not prove unlimited bandwidth/perfect fidelity.
Missing modulation despite LED DC brightness is a consistent fault; a targeted upstream or driver-output test distinguishes it.
records.scoring: 4+8+4=16, passing10. The middle unit is explicitly8 or0 with all essential evidence requirements. Without observed actual build/own measurements in S (or required interpretation in D), at most8 remains, so the assessment cannot pass under its written scoring contract.
records.modes: Teacher selects S/D before work. S requires real observation and own data, not a textual claim. D is an interpretation assessment and explicitly certifies no personal build.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Zwei Lichtkanäle auf einem Weg trennen
records.summary: A fully specified two-colour model permits independent design and exact reconstruction of two channels, then a meaningful loss-of-distinguishability test. It stays at model-experiment design, not industrial multiplexer construction.
material: Two independently controlled narrow spectral bands, combiner, common fibre, splitter and ideal filters supply the necessary construction choices.
A supplied model source is appropriate to the source-assisted development competence; actual physical assembly is not falsely claimed.
solution: Input sequences A=1010,B=0110 give red/blue/red+blue/dark; matching filters recover each original sequence.
With equal-intensity same-colour sources and no extra coding, the aggregate level cannot distinguish10 from01; the solution explicitly does not rule out different coding schemes.
Nonideal out-of-band filter transmission is an appropriate crosstalk mechanism.
records.scoring: 5+4+3=12, passing8. Construction, channel evidence and model-limit points correspond to the three tasks; exchanged channel names are properly accepted.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Einen gespeicherten Schaltzustand ändern
records.summary: The supplied cross-coupled npn topology really supports the two stated stable model states and the described set/reset pulse sequence. It does not confuse a bistable latch with an oscillator.
material: C1→47 kΩ→B2 and C2→47 kΩ→B1 form positive mutual feedback through two inverting stages.

Low collector≈0.2 V keeps the other transistor off; the off collector≈4.8 V can supply the opposite base through its resistor under the explicit adequate-gain assumption. The high level is plausible given the2.2-kΩ/47-kΩ loading, not an ideal unconnected5 V claim.
Buttons only pull individual bases low; simultaneous activation and detailed start transients are excluded.
solution: T1 on/T2 off gives Q=C2 high; reversed state gives Q low.
P1 pulls B1 low, T1 off, C1 high, T2 on, C2 low; feedback retains the new state after release. P2 reverses it.
Undefined power-on state without initialization is correctly limited; no astable or universal flip-flop claim.
records.scoring: 5+4+3=12, passing8; Q-state, causal sequence and persistence are explicitly credited rather than a memorized label alone.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Eine Elemententstehungs-Behauptung prüfen
records.summary: The argument task distinguishes nucleosynthesis from transport and detection location. Its material supports the expected criticism without requiring invented source attribution or memorized full fusion chains.
material: C/O formation in suitable stellar phases and neutron-capture production beyond the iron region are appropriate bounded descriptions.
M2 arrows denote transport/mixing, not further nuclear reactions. Detection in a younger system is not proof of formation there.
The text does not assert that every star/supernova creates every heavy element, nor that a single neutron-capture environment is exclusive.
solution: Co-occurrence of carbon/gold does not establish their direct production by the current star through simple hydrogen fusion.
Prior synthesis, expulsion/release, mixing and later system formation provide the requested materially supported alternative.
Abundance/isotope or age information can constrain hypotheses but cannot uniquely name an earlier progenitor from the given material.
records.scoring: 5+4+3=12, passing8; premise/inference, production/transport and evidence limits are meaningfully separated. No quantitative fusion-chain result is claimed by these points.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Bedingte Stern-Endstadien prognostizieren
records.summary: The quantitative inputs and conditional stellar-remnant predictions are internally consistent and distinguish initial mass, early total remaining mass and compact-remnant mass. The threshold is explicitly a model assumption.
material: Early subtraction gives0.6,10,16 M☉; B/C separately supply1.6/5.0 M☉ compact remnants, so no second subtraction is justified.
A names a supported C/O core; B names a stable neutron-rich remnant; C states fallback and an assumed2.3-M☉ neutron-star limit.
solution: A→white dwarf, B→neutron star, C→black hole follow the supplied evolutionary evidence, not initial mass alone.
Equal initial18 M☉ in B/C can yield different remnants because their loss/core/ejection/fallback histories differ.
The2.1–2.5 interval straddles2.3; the permissible answer is conditional, with equality explicitly unresolved. No universal initial-mass cutoff is claimed.
records.scoring: 3+5+4=12, passing8. Correct arithmetic is insufficient alone; quantity distinction, evolutionary reasoning and conditional uncertainty carry the majority of points.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Neutronensteuerung und Wärmeabfuhr im Reaktor
records.summary: The task correctly separates neutron moderation/control from heat removal in a deliberately simplified thermal-reactor model. It is explanatory paper work, not reactor construction or operation.
material: Fuel fission produces new neutrons and heat; moderation slows rather than predominantly absorbs, while control rods absorb.
Coolant/pump/heat exchanger form the heat-transfer path; omitted passive safety and real design variation are stated.
Decay heat after shutdown is explicitly supplied as information, so the safety-limit answer is not an unexplained extra demand.
solution: Deeper rod insertion increases absorption and reduces chain continuation within the model.
Pump failure first affects forced heat transport and is not equivalent to neutron absorption; the solution avoids an unjustified specific real-power or feedback prediction.
Stopping the chain does not immediately eliminate decay heat; quantitative residual-heat and real-system data are absent.
records.scoring: 6+4+2=12, passing8. Four components, causal coordination and neutron-versus-heat distinction are credited; transfer compares distinct component functions.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Arbeitspunkt und Verzerrung einer Emitterschaltung
records.summary: The supplied common-emitter table, bias points and clipping limits define a solvable amplifier task. All current numerical results are correct; phase inversion is circuit-specific and supply energy is not created in the base branch.
material: For the active model I_C=100 I_B and1-kΩ collector resistor imply U_C=10 V−I_C R_C; every table column matches.
Output limits0.2/10 V and provided bias avoid an underdetermined bias-network calculation.
solution: At50 µA:5 V;40/60 µA:6/4 V. A±10-µA change controls±1 mA and inverted±1 V.
At50±60 µA, unconstrained extrapolation would give−10/110 µA and11/−1 V; cutoff/saturation constrain the actual waveform.

At80 µA the2-V bias leaves1.8 V downward versus8 V upward. A±30-µA input clips downward; shifting to50 µA yields20–80 µA and8–2 V without clipping. Reducing amplitude is only accepted with explicit surrender of the original amplitude demand.
records.scoring: 5+4+3=12, passing8; limits and bias transfer are assessed in addition to arithmetic.

records.title: Prüfungsaufgabe: Einen Transistor als Schalter deuten
records.summary: The revised switching task supplies a complete low-voltage npn/LED circuit, a qualitative thin-base transport model and an honest S/D evidence branch. It does not substitute two isolated diodes or a mechanical contact for transistor action.
material: Common0 V, explicit B/C/E pin identification,10-kΩ base and330-Ω LED resistors make both paths explicit.

Demonstration values are plausible:0.42 mA through10 kΩ leaves about0.8 V at B-E;8.1 mA through330 Ω leaves about2.33 V for LED+C-E. The task does not treat those inferred residuals as universal fixed device values.
Current-limited checked5-V teaching supply and power-off reconnects are proportionate safeguards.
solution: Control and load paths, thin-base role and supply energy are correctly distinguished.
The supplied off/on/open-base observations support electronic switching, not a universal constant gain from two points.
Sensor5 V in light turns the LED on; reversing the sensor response reverses the states.
records.scoring: 4+8+4=16, passing10. The mode-evidence unit is indivisible8/0; without the observed working setup, own on/off/current data and control test required by S, or full D interpretation, only8 remains.
